messages:
elaine: quick triage — onboarding Novus-Mini v2.7B. License text includes `Non-Commercial use only` + an `Attribution` clause and a line that says 'no redistribution of modified weights or binaries'. Can we: 1) ship quantized weights to customers on Dedicated? 2) serve embeddings to paying customers if model is used server-side? 3) show model attribution in the UI (required placement/wording)?
jamal (legal): short answer: probably not for commercial paid hosting. NC = big red flag. Quantized weights are almost certainly a derivative/binary -> falls under "no redistribution". Serving (SaaS) sometimes still counted as use, depends on license wording. Need exact license link. Do we have the upstream license URL?
mika: adding some nuance — from an infra/ML perspective: if we never hand out the quantized file (i.e., only run inference in our runtime), that's less like redistribution and more like "use". But some NC clauses forbid use for commercial purposes regardless of distribution. If license text says "no redistribution of modified binaries" then creating and distributing quantized binaries to a customer is almost certainly disallowed.
elaine: license: https://example.org/novus-mini/LICENSE (copied snippet: "Model weights and modified binaries may not be redistributed for commercial purposes. Attribution must be displayed where model outputs are shown.")
jamal (legal): thanks. Given that wording: - Hosting the model in our hosted API for paying customers = commercial use -> disallowed. - Dedicated/reserved GPU pools where we transfer a quantized file to customer = redistribution -> disallowed. - Private deployments where the customer supplies the original weights (BYOW) and we deliver only orchestration/ops is probably okay (but confirm with compliance).
mika: for embeddings specifically: the license restricts model weights/binaries. Many licenses have separate rules for model outputs; this one ties attribution to outputs though. If the license doesn't explicitly prohibit generating embeddings for commercial use, it's still risky because it was written to control downstream commercial exploitation. I'd treat embeddings for paying customers as prohibited until we confirm.
tom-infra: operationally, we could offer a "self-hosted Private" plan where customer brings their own weights. We must add a clear documentation flow: they attest they have commercial rights. That avoids us redistributing quantized weights. We already have a BYOW onboarding flow — can reuse that.
jamal (legal): recommend options: (A) request a commercial license from upstream; (B) ask upstream to add a permissive redistribution exception; (C) only allow research/internal evals and BYOW private deployments; (D) if customer is non-commercial edu org, we can allow hosted inference after a written attestation.
elaine: for attribution: license requires it shown where model outputs are displayed. Do we need exact copy? Is a footer line enough?
jamal (legal): attribution needs to be "prominent" per text. We should: 1) include model name + link near the feature UI (e.g., "Responses powered by Novus-Mini v2.7B — license: <link>") and 2) include the same in API response headers/usage docs for developer customers. I'll draft a short attribution template.
mika: small quant experiment question — if we quantize only at runtime (no persisted quant file) using on-the-fly kernels, does that help? Technically it's still a transformed representation of weights in memory -> could be considered a derivative. Legally ambiguous.
jamal (legal): yep ambiguous. Better to avoid relying on that for commercial hosting.
elaine: ok. next steps: jamal, can you draft a short legal guidance blurb we can paste into the onboarding checklist? mika/tom can put guardrails in BYOW and private plans.
jamal (legal): will do. Draft will include: allowed/disallowed uses, attribution template, and suggested customer attestation for BYOW. ETA: today EOD.
opsbot: tag added: #legal-triage :white_check_mark:
elaine: thanks everyone — copying product so they don't try to enable this in Hosted without a license. I'll pause the ML eval run for commercial benchmarks.
